parallels.title: The man with the withered hand
Jairus’ daughter and the woman who touched his garment
The boy with an unclean spirit
The signs of the end (the Olivet discourse)

traces.intro: Seven times in John, Jesus says “I am” with a predicate — each one a claim about who he is. Behind them stands the absolute “I am” of John 8:58 (“Before Abraham was, I am”), echoing the name God gave Moses in Exodus 3:14.

items.label: I am the bread of life
items.note: Spoken the day after the feeding of the five thousand. As manna sustained Israel, he sustains all who come to him — and “shall never hunger.”

items.label: I am the light of the world
items.note: Said at the Feast of Tabernacles, when the great lamps lit the temple courts. In him there is no darkness at all.

items.label: I am the door
items.note: The sheepfold had one opening, guarded by the shepherd himself. Every approach to God goes through him.

items.label: I am the good shepherd
items.note: The shepherd who does not run from the wolf but lays down his life for the sheep — a direct prophecy of the cross.

items.label: I am the resurrection, and the life
items.note: Said at the tomb of Lazarus, moments before calling him out. Resurrection is not only an event; it is a person.

items.label: I am the way, and the truth, and the life
items.note: The most exclusive claim ever made: no one comes to the Father except through him.

items.label: I am the true vine
items.note: Israel was God's vine (Psalm 80, Isaiah 5). Jesus declares himself the true one — life flows only by abiding in him.

traces.title: The seven “I AM” sayings

traces.intro: John stacks titles for Jesus from the first chapter to the last — each one opening a different window onto who he is.

items.label: The Word
items.note: In the beginning was the Word — eternal, divine, the agent of creation itself.

items.label: The Lamb of God
items.note: John the Baptist's announcement: the Passover lamb to whom every sacrifice pointed, come to take away the sin of the world.

items.label: The Son of God
items.note: The Baptist's witness, confirmed by the Father's voice at the baptism.

items.label: The Messiah (the Christ)
items.note: Andrew's confession: the long-promised Anointed One has been found.

items.label: The King of Israel
items.note: Nathanael's confession under the fig tree — fulfilled openly at the triumphal entry (12:13).

items.label: The Son of Man
items.note: Jesus' own favorite title, drawn from Daniel 7:13 — the heavenly figure given everlasting dominion.

items.label: The Saviour of the world
items.note: The Samaritans' confession: salvation is not for one nation only.

items.label: The Holy One of God
items.note: Peter's confession when many disciples walked away — “Lord, to whom shall we go?”

items.label: Sanctified and sent by the Father
items.note: Consecrated for his mission — the Sent One, in John's constant language.

items.label: My Lord and my God
items.note: Thomas's climax: the Gospel's highest confession, and Jesus blesses all who believe without seeing.

traces.title: Titles of Christ in John

traces.intro: John keeps pausing the narrative to say “that the scripture might be fulfilled.” Here are the promise-and-fulfillment pairs, mostly clustered around the cross.

items.label: They part my garments — Psalm 22:18
items.note: The soldiers divide his clothes and cast lots for his tunic, exactly as the psalm described a thousand years earlier.

items.label: Vinegar to drink — Psalm 69:21
items.note: “I thirst” — spoken, John says, so that even this detail of the psalm would be fulfilled.

items.label: Not a bone broken — Exodus 12:46; Psalm 34:20
items.note: The Passover lamb's bones were not to be broken. Neither were his.

items.label: They shall look on him whom they pierced — Zechariah 12:10
items.note: The spear, the blood and water — Zechariah's pierced one, mourned like an only son.

items.label: Thy king cometh on a colt — Zechariah 9:9
items.note: The triumphal entry rides straight out of Zechariah's prophecy.

items.label: Zeal for thy house — Psalm 69:9
items.note: The disciples remembered this psalm as Jesus drove the traders from the temple.

items.label: Betrayed by a friend — Psalm 41:9
items.note: “He that eateth my bread lifted up his heel against me” — Judas at the table.

items.label: Hated without a cause — Psalm 35:19; 69:4
items.note: The world's hatred of Jesus fulfills the psalms of the righteous sufferer.

items.label: Who hath believed our report? — Isaiah 53:1
items.note: Isaiah's suffering-servant chapter explains Israel's unbelief — and identifies Jesus as the servant.

traces.title: Prophecies fulfilled

traces.intro: John calls Jesus' miracles “signs” — each one points past itself to who he is. John 20:31 says they were written “that ye may believe.”

items.label: Water into wine at Cana
items.note: The first sign: the master of the feast tastes the new wine of the kingdom.

items.label: Healing the nobleman's son
items.note: Healed from a distance by a word — faith without sight, honored.

items.label: The paralytic at Bethesda
items.note: Thirty-eight years waiting by the pool; one word — “Arise” — and he walks.

items.label: Feeding the five thousand
items.note: The only miracle in all four Gospels — the new manna, pointing to the Bread of Life.

items.label: Walking on the water
items.note: “It is I” — literally “I am” — and the wind ceases.

items.label: Healing the man born blind
items.note: Mud, Siloam, and sight — the Light of the World giving light to dark eyes.

items.label: Raising Lazarus
items.note: Four days dead, and the Resurrection calls him out — the sign that sealed Jesus' own death sentence.

traces.title: The seven signs

traces.intro: If you read nothing else: the twelve verses that carry the whole Gospel, from eternity past to the reason it was written.

items.label: For God so loved the world
The way, the truth, the life

traces.title: The spine of John — 12 verses
Matthew’s “that it might be fulfilled”
traces.intro: Matthew writes for readers who knew the Scriptures, and again and again he stops the story to show an Old Testament word coming true in Jesus.

items.label: Born of a virgin — “God with us”
items.note: Isaiah 7:14: Immanuel, given as a sign to the house of David.

items.label: Born in Bethlehem
items.note: Micah 5:2: a ruler from the small town of Judah, David’s birthplace.

items.label: Called out of Egypt
items.note: Hosea 11:1: what was said of Israel the son is lived out by Jesus the Son.

items.label: Rachel weeping for her children
items.note: Jeremiah 31:15: the grief of exile echoes in Herod’s massacre at Bethlehem.

items.label: He shall be called a Nazarene
items.note: Matthew cites “the prophets” in general — likely a wordplay on the Branch (Hebrew netzer) of Isaiah 11:1.

items.label: The voice in the wilderness
items.note: Isaiah 40:3: John the Baptist prepares the way of the Lord.

items.label: A great light in Galilee of the Gentiles
items.note: Isaiah 9:1-2: the ministry begins in the region the prophet said would see the light first.

items.label: He took our infirmities
items.note: Isaiah 53:4: the healings are a foretaste of the Servant who bears our griefs.

items.label: My servant, in whom my soul is well pleased
items.note: Isaiah 42:1-4: the gentle Servant who will not break a bruised reed.

items.label: Hearing but not understanding
items.note: Isaiah 6:9-10: the parables divide those who will hear from those who will not.

items.label: Speaking in parables
items.note: Psalm 78:2: things hidden from the foundation of the world, opened in stories.

items.label: Your King comes, meek, on a donkey
items.note: Zechariah 9:9: the entry into Jerusalem, acted out deliberately.

items.label: Thirty pieces of silver
items.note: Zechariah 11:12-13 (with Jeremiah’s potter): the price set on him, thrown to the potter.

traces.title: The parables of Jesus
traces.intro: Jesus taught the kingdom of God in stories drawn from fields, kitchens, vineyards and family life. These are the best known, in the order they appear.

items.label: The sower
items.note: Four soils, one seed: how the word is received decides what it bears. Also Mark 4 and Luke 8.

items.label: The seed growing secretly
items.note: The kingdom grows “he knoweth not how” — Mark’s own parable.

items.label: The wheat and the tares
items.note: Good and evil grow together until the harvest; judgment belongs to the Lord of the harvest.

items.label: The mustard seed
items.note: The smallest of seeds becomes a tree the birds can nest in.

items.label: The leaven
items.note: Hidden in three measures of meal until the whole is leavened.

items.label: The hidden treasure and the pearl
items.note: The kingdom is worth everything a person has — and gladly.

items.label: The unforgiving servant
items.note: Forgiven a debt he could never pay, he will not forgive a small one.

items.label: The labourers in the vineyard
items.note: The last hired are paid the same: grace, not wages.

items.label: The wicked husbandmen
items.note: Tenants who kill the owner’s son — Jesus tells Israel’s leaders the story of his own death. Also Mark 12 and Luke 20.

items.label: The wedding feast
items.note: The invited refuse; the streets are filled; a wedding garment is required.

items.label: The ten virgins
items.note: Five ready, five not: watch, for you do not know the day.

items.label: The talents
items.note: What the servants did with what was entrusted to them.

items.label: The sheep and the goats
items.note: The King counts mercy shown to “the least of these” as shown to himself.

items.label: The good Samaritan
items.note: “Who is my neighbour?” answered by an outsider who shows mercy.

items.label: The rich fool
items.note: Bigger barns, and a soul required that very night.

items.label: The lost sheep
items.note: The shepherd leaves the ninety and nine; heaven rejoices over one.

items.label: The lost coin
items.note: A woman sweeps the whole house for one coin.

items.label: The prodigal son
items.note: A father runs to a returning son — and pleads with the elder brother too.

items.label: The rich man and Lazarus
items.note: A great gulf fixed, and a warning that even one risen from the dead may not persuade.

items.label: The persistent widow
items.note: Always pray and do not lose heart.

items.label: The Pharisee and the publican
items.note: “God, be thou merciful to me a sinner” — and he went home justified.

traces.title: The mighty works in Mark
traces.intro: Mark is the fastest Gospel — “straightway” after “straightway” — and much of its first half is a rush of healings and wonders that make people ask, “Who then is this?”

items.label: An unclean spirit silenced
items.note: Teaching with authority, and the spirits obey.

items.label: Peter’s mother-in-law
items.note: He takes her by the hand, and she rises to serve.

items.label: A leper made clean
items.note: Jesus touches the untouchable: “I will; be thou made clean.”

items.label: The paralytic through the roof
items.note: Forgiving sins first, then healing to prove the authority to forgive.

items.label: The withered hand on the sabbath
items.note: Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath?

items.label: Calming the storm
items.note: “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

items.label: Legion
items.note: A man no chains could hold, found clothed and in his right mind.

items.label: A daughter raised, a woman healed
items.note: Twelve years of bleeding, a girl of twelve years — “Talitha cumi.”

items.label: Five thousand fed
items.note: Shepherd of sheep without a shepherd, he makes them sit on the green grass.

items.label: Walking on the sea
items.note: “Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.”

items.label: The Syrophoenician woman
items.note: Even the dogs eat the children’s crumbs — faith from a Gentile mother.

items.label: “Ephphatha” — be opened
items.note: A deaf man hears and speaks; “He hath done all things well.”

items.label: Four thousand fed
items.note: Compassion again, this time in Gentile country.

items.label: The blind man at Bethsaida
items.note: Healed in two stages — just before the disciples’ own eyes are opened at Caesarea Philippi.

items.label: The boy with a spirit
items.note: “I believe; help thou mine unbelief.”

items.label: Blind Bartimaeus
items.note: “Son of David, have mercy on me” — he follows Jesus in the way.

traces.title: Promises of the Messiah
traces.intro: Long before Bethlehem, the Old Testament speaks of one who would come — a seed, a prophet, a king, a servant. Each item notes where the New Testament says the promise was kept.

items.label: The seed of the woman
items.note: The first promise: the serpent’s head bruised by her seed. Compare Romans 16:20 and Galatians 4:4.

items.label: All the families of the earth blessed
items.note: Through Abraham’s seed — Paul says that seed is Christ (Galatians 3:8, 16).

items.label: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah
items.note: A ruler from Judah to whom the peoples will gather; Revelation 5:5 calls Jesus the Lion of the tribe of Judah.

items.label: A star out of Jacob
items.note: Balaam sees a sceptre rising out of Israel — far off.

items.label: A prophet like Moses
items.note: Peter applies it to Jesus in Acts 3:22-23.

items.label: David’s son on an everlasting throne
items.note: Gabriel echoes it to Mary: “the throne of his father David” (Luke 1:32-33).

items.label: “Thou art my Son”
items.note: Quoted of Jesus’ resurrection in Acts 13:33 and of his rank above the angels in Hebrews 1:5.

items.label: Not abandoned to Sheol
items.note: Peter at Pentecost: David spoke of the resurrection of the Christ (Acts 2:25-31).

items.label: Hands and feet pierced, garments divided
items.note: The cross described in a psalm of David; John 19:24 quotes the lots cast for his clothing.

items.label: “Sit thou at my right hand”
items.note: The most quoted Old Testament verse in the New — Jesus uses it himself (Matthew 22:44).

items.label: A virgin shall conceive
items.note: Immanuel — Matthew 1:23.

items.label: Unto us a child is born
items.note: Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace, on David’s throne for ever.

items.label: A shoot out of the stock of Jesse
items.note: The Spirit rests on him; Paul quotes it in Romans 15:12.

items.label: Prepare ye the way of Jehovah
items.note: All four Gospels open Jesus’ ministry with this voice (e.g. Mark 1:3).

items.label: The suffering Servant
items.note: Wounded for our transgressions — Philip explains this passage to the Ethiopian (Acts 8:32-35).

items.label: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me
items.note: Jesus reads it in Nazareth and says, “To-day hath this scripture been fulfilled” (Luke 4:18-21).

items.label: The righteous Branch
items.note: A king from David called “Jehovah our righteousness.”

items.label: A new covenant
items.note: Written on the heart; Jesus speaks of “the new covenant in my blood” (Luke 22:20; Hebrews 8:8-12).

items.label: One like a son of man
items.note: Coming with the clouds to receive an everlasting kingdom — Jesus’ answer at his trial (Mark 14:62).

items.label: Out of Bethlehem
items.note: Ephrathah, little among the thousands of Judah (Matthew 2:6).

items.label: Your King, riding on a donkey
items.note: Just and having salvation, lowly (John 12:14-15).

items.label: They shall look on him whom they pierced
items.note: John sees it fulfilled at the cross (John 19:37).

items.label: My messenger before my face
items.note: Mark opens with it: John the Baptist is the messenger (Mark 1:2).

traces.title: Psalms the New Testament reads of Christ
traces.intro: The apostles found Jesus all through the Psalms — Israel’s songbook became the church’s first commentary on the cross and the resurrection.

items.label: “Thou art my Son”
items.note: Hebrews 1:5; Acts 13:33.

items.label: All things put under his feet
items.note: Hebrews 2:6-9 sees Jesus as the man crowned with glory.

items.label: Thou wilt not leave my soul to Sheol
items.note: Acts 2:27; 13:35 — the resurrection.

items.label: “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?”
items.note: Jesus’ own cry from the cross (Matthew 27:46).

items.label: They part my garments among them
items.note: John 19:24.

items.label: Lo, I am come to do thy will
items.note: Hebrews 10:5-7: the body prepared for the one sacrifice.

items.label: He that ate of my bread hath lifted up his heel
items.note: Jesus applies it to Judas (John 13:18).

items.label: Thy throne, O God, is for ever
items.note: Hebrews 1:8-9: said to the Son.

items.label: The zeal of thy house
items.note: The disciples remember it at the temple cleansing (John 2:17).

items.label: In my thirst they gave me vinegar
A priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek
items.note: Hebrews 5:6; 7:17.

items.label: The stone the builders rejected
items.note: Jesus quotes it of himself (Matthew 21:42); Peter too (Acts 4:11).

items.label: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Jehovah
items.note: The crowds’ cry on Palm Sunday (Matthew 21:9).

traces.title: Christ in the hymns of the early church
traces.intro: Some passages in the letters read like the first Christian songs and creeds — compact, poetic summaries of who Jesus is and what he did.

items.label: In the form of God, he emptied himself
items.note: From equality with God to the cross, and then the name above every name.

items.label: The image of the invisible God
items.note: Firstborn of all creation and from the dead; in him all things hold together.

items.label: The effulgence of his glory
items.note: God has spoken last and best in a Son, who upholds all things and sat down on high.

items.label: Great is the mystery of godliness
items.note: Manifested in the flesh, received up in glory — a six-line creed.

items.label: By whose stripes ye were healed
items.note: Peter weaves Isaiah 53 into a pattern for suffering believers.

items.label: Him who knew no sin he made to be sin
items.note: The great exchange, in a single sentence.

items.label: Worthy is the Lamb
items.note: The new song of heaven to the Lamb that was slain.
